description: The core cross-field rule (CONSTRAINT_INVALIDATES_PASS): a result CANNOT have both passed=true and a constraint_violations entry with invalidates_result=true -- that combination is the exact failure mode this field exists to prevent (a consumer trusting `passed` alone would count a disqualified result as a success). Unlike SELF_PARENT (Discussion #45) and DUPLICATE_ATTEMPT (Discussion #22), which genuinely need a $data reference this project's schemas don't use, this rule is a conditional against a constant and IS expressible in plain JSON Schema via if/contains/then/const (Draft 7+; see schema/resultset.json's results[].items.allOf). As of that fix, both validation paths agree: this fixture's `expect.valid: false` holds against the hand-rolled validators (validate_result_set / validateResultSet) AND against the raw JSON Schema itself -- a stronger conformance statement than this project's schemas previously guaranteed. Credit: MSKazemi, https://github.com/adhabnr-ux/evalport/pull/48#issuecomment-5639403956. See sdk/python/tests/test_schema_consistency.py's mirrored test for the explicit regression coverage of both paths agreeing.
